Abstract Accurate and effective biomarkers for continuous monitoring of graft function are needed after kidney transplantation. The aim of this study was to establish a circulating exosomal miRNA panel as non‐invasive biomarker for kidney transplant recipients. Plasma exosomes of 58 kidney transplant recipients and 27 healthy controls were extracted by gel exclusion chromatography and characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis and Western blotting. Post‐transplant renal graft function was evaluated by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Quantitative real‐time polymerase chain reaction was used to determine the expression of exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs). Exosomal miR‐21, miR‐210 and miR‐4639 showed negative correlations with eGFR in the training set and were selected for further analysis. In the validation set, miR‐21, miR‐210 and miR‐4639 showed the capability to discriminate between subjects with chronic allograft dysfunction (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ) and those with normal graft function (eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ). Three‐miRNA panel exhibited higher accuracy compared with individual miRNAs or double indicators. One‐year follow‐up revealed a stable recovery of allograft function in subjects with low calculated score from three‐miRNA panel (below the optimal cut‐off value). J Cell Mol Med . 2020 ; 24 : 12154 – 12163 . 10.1111/jcmm.15861 Funding information The work was supported by Jiangsu Provincial 333 Department Support project (BRA2017116) and Changzhou Municipal Science and Technology Bureau Support project (CE20175030). 1 INTRODUCTION Since the first successful kidney transplant in 1954, kidney transplantation has become the routine management for patients presenting with end‐stage renal disease. 1 The application of highly effective immunosuppressive drugs over the past 20 years has significantly improved the 1‐year survival of kidney grafts. 2 However, chronic allograft dysfunction, which may due to both immunologic and non‐immunologic factors, is the major cause of renal allograft loss in the long‐term. 3 , 4 Thus, accurate assessment and monitoring of allograft function is critical for kidney transplant recipients. Currently, measurements of serum creatinine (Cr), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and proteinuria are often applied for the evaluation of progression of kidney injury. 5 The gold standard test is histological diagnosis with a renal transplant biopsy. 6 However, there are some disadvantages of low specificity and sensitivity or invasiveness during the evaluation. Cr is derived from the non‐enzymatic dehydration of skeletal muscle creatine, which itself is generated from amino acids in the liver. 7 Thus, numerous factors such as muscle mass and turnover, sex, diet, race, liver function and medication use can influence serum Cr concentration. 8 In kidney transplant recipients, serum Cr concentration can be affected due to the long‐term use of corticosteroids, infection, acute rejection and previous prolonged haemodialysis therapy. 7 As a result, the Cr‐based eGFR estimation equation is also flawed, and the evaluation equation itself is not perfect. 9 Moreover, proteinuria can be affected by exercise and diet. 10 Kidney biopsies are considered to be the gold standard for evaluating allograft dysfunction. However, renal biopsy cannot be used to monitor the progression of injury because it is an invasive procedure and cannot be performed serially. 11 Furthermore, the histological evaluation of biopsies is subjective and samples removed from one segment of the transplanted kidney may not represent the whole graft. 12 Therefore, it is necessary to find a sensitive and non‐invasive biomarker for the continuous monitoring of graft function after kidney transplantation. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a group of small non‐coding RNAs that can regulate up to 60% of gene expression in mammals by binding to the 3′ untranslated region (3′‐UTR) of the target messenger RNA (mRNA) involved in many diseases. 13 Exosomes are small (40‐160 nm) membrane vesicles of endocytic origin that are released into the extracellular environment on fusion of multivesicular bodies with the plasma membrane. 14 , 15 Exosomal miRNAs are proved to be stably expressed in serum, plasma, urine, saliva and other body fluids. 16 Many studies have indicated that levels of exosomal miRNAs are associated with renal function. For instance, the differential expression of five miRNAs (miR‐32, miR‐107, miR‐142‐3p, miR‐204 and miR‐211) in patients with chronic allograft dysfunction was confirmed by using an independent set of kidney tissue samples and paired urine samples. 17 Moreover, five miRNAs (miR‐200b, miR‐375, miR‐423‐5p, miR‐193b and miR‐345) were identified as potential biomarkers for monitoring allograft function in the urine samples of renal transplant recipients. 18 However, the role of circulating exosomal miRNAs in the monitoring of post‐transplant renal graft function has not been fully figured out. In this study, we examined correlations between exosomal miRNA levels and eGFR in cohorts of kidney transplant recipients and healthy controls. A circulating exosomal miRNA panel was established as the non‐invasive biomarker for monitoring of post‐transplant renal graft function in the 1‐year follow‐up. extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic and predictive value of a circulating exosomal microRNA (miRNA) panel, specifically comprising miR-21-5p, miR-210-3p, and miR-4639-5p, as non-invasive biomarkers for monitoring post-transplant renal graft function in kidney transplant recipients. The findings demonstrated that these miRNAs were negatively correlated with eGFR and elevated in chronic allograft dysfunction, with the combined three-miRNA panel exhibiting superior diagnostic potential for predicting disease progression and long-term graft function, including future eGFR recovery, compared to individual miRNAs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-transplant renal graft function monitoring using a circulating exosomal miRNA panel
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focused on the monitoring of post-transplant renal graft function using a panel of three exosomal miRNAs (miR-21, miR-210, miR-4639). Plasma samples were collected from 58 kidney transplant recipients and 27 healthy controls at 3 months post-transplantation and during a 1-year longitudinal follow-up (at 3, 6, and 12 months). Renal function was stratified by eGFR levels (<60, 60-90, >=90 mL/min/1.73 m2) to compare chronic allograft dysfunction (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) against normal graft function (eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). No therapeutic dose-response comparisons or specific intervention details related to the transplant procedure were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Exosomal microRNA expression (quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction or qRT-PCR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed significant negative correlations with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (r = -0.5324, P < .0001). Levels were significantly higher in transplant recipients with chronic allograft dysfunction (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) compared to those with normal graft function (eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). Significant differences also observed between eGFR >= 90 and 60 <= eGFR < 90 (P < .05). AUC = 0.78 for discriminating between chronic allograft dysfunction and normal graft function. Patients with impaired renal function tended to have elevated miR-21 expression.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: MicroRNA involved in gene regulation, associated with kidney transplantation, renal function, and hypoxia/ischaemia conditions. It modulates renal function and participates in the pathogenesis of renal diseases.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant renal graft function monitoring, particularly in distinguishing chronic allograft dysfunction from normal function. Also relevant in impaired renal function, diabetic kidney disease, chronic kidney disease, glomerular injury, and as a component of a three-miRNA panel.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with eGFR and renal function, indicating chronic allograft dysfunction. Has predictive value for delayed graft function following kidney transplantation and serves as a non-invasive biomarker for monitoring post-transplant renal graft function.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: MicroRNA involved in gene regulation, associated with kidney transplantation, renal function, and hypoxia/ischaemia conditions. Participates in cellular oxidative stress responses and is enriched in human plasma exosomes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant renal graft function monitoring, particularly in distinguishing chronic allograft dysfunction from normal function, and as a component of a three-miRNA panel.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with eGFR and renal function, indicating chronic allograft dysfunction. Facilitates biomarker discovery and serves as a non-invasive biomarker for monitoring post-transplant renal graft function and predicting disease progression.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Combined exosomal microRNA expression (calculated score from panel members via logistic regression model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased diagnostic sensitivity and specificity; higher accuracy
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exhibited higher accuracy (AUC = 0.89; 95% CI, 0.80-0.97) compared with individual miRNAs or double indicators for discriminating chronic allograft dysfunction (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) from normal graft function (eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). Achieved diagnostic sensitivity of 88.46% and specificity of 73.08% using an optimal cut-off value of 0.43. Subjects with a low calculated score from the panel (below the optimal cut-off value) showed stable recovery of allograft function during a one-year follow-up.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Collective regulation of gene expression, acting as a combined indicator of renal graft health. Provides enhanced diagnostic and predictive power for renal function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring post-transplant renal graft function in kidney transplant recipients, particularly for discriminating chronic allograft dysfunction from normal graft function.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: An effective, non-invasive biomarker panel for monitoring post-transplant renal graft function, offering higher accuracy for predicting allograft dysfunction and indicating stable recovery. The score of this three-miRNA panel may predict future eGFR recovery and improvement of post-transplant renal graft function.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not specifically quantified in this context; described as closely related to disease status and serving as disease biomarkers with differential expression.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulation of gene expression; carriers of intracellular biological information, crucial in various disease etiologies.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Associated with various renal conditions including post-transplant renal graft function, tubulointerstitial inflammation, renal fibrosis, ischaemic kidney injury, IgA nephropathy, acute kidney injury, and chronic kidney disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts disease progression, aids in determining therapeutic strategies, and indicates presence/pathogenesis of various renal diseases. Useful for continuous monitoring of graft function.
